newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish prisoner escapes after wielding syringe.
newsitem.headline: Irish prisoner escapes after wielding syringe.

text.p: Irish police hunted on Monday for a convicted drug dealer who escaped from a prison van after threatening a prison officer with a blood-filled syringe.

Michael Cahill, who was serving 4 1/2 years for drugs offences, was being transferred to Cork prison following a fracas in Dublin's Mountjoy jail when he suddenly produced a syringe and held it to the neck of the prison officer handcuffed to him.
He then demanded that two other officers unlock his handcuffs and open the doors of the van, allowing him to escape on foot toward Dublin.
Cahill is a brother of former leading Irish crime world boss, Martin Cahill, who was shot dead at the wheel of his car in Dublin two years ago.
Ireland's justice ministry is expected to hold an inquiry into Cahill's escape and whether the fracas which led to his transfer was staged or genuine.
